children.translated_text: He by whose rays of speech the heart-lotus of those beginning with me — deluded without remainder —
blossoms forth — I bow to that Supreme Person. (1)

children.text: pāramiṃ guhyamantraṃ ca śritvā bodhiḥ prasidhyati /
children.translated_text: Through hearing the <s>Pāramitā</s> and the secret <s>Mantra</s> [vehicles], awakening is accomplished.
Since the <s>Guru</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>, has spoken thus, the meaning of that is written by me. (2)
The secret <s>Mantra</s> [vehicle] is not spoken of here; the conduct of the <s>Pāramitā</s> path —
the conduct of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — I shall write in brief. (3)
The wise one should take vows, with <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) as the foremost.
Having examined all the <s>sūtras</s>, one should hear the <s>śāstras</s> in their entirety. (4)

children.text: kāyena manasā vācā yathoktān saṃvarān tribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: By body, mind, and speech — the three — one should guard the vows as prescribed,
keeping them unbroken and pure, and should purify one's moral conduct. (5)
One should know the proper measure of food, and should guard the doors of the sense faculties.

children.text: rātreḥ pūrve 'pare bhāge na suptvā yogamācaret || 6 ||
children.translated_text: In the first and last watches of the night, without sleeping, one should practice <s>yoga</s>. (6)
One should be exceedingly fearful even of the slightest faults.

children.text: rātrerbhāgatrayaṃ kṛtvā hyantye bhāge tu jāgṛyāt || 7 ||
children.translated_text: Having divided the night into three parts, in the last part one should keep vigil. (7)
One should wash the face and so on, or rinsing may also be done.
Seated in a comfortable posture, one should recollect the true nature of <s>dharmas</s>. (8)
When unable [to meditate] due to disturbance by signs [of distraction], then rising and [contemplating] apparent objects
as being like an illusion — in the intervals [one should practice] meritorious yogas. (9)
One should fulfill the seven-limbed [worship] and practice the vast aspiration prayer.

children.text: bhāvayed bhāvanāṃ pūrvā kāle 'tha bhojanasya ca || 10 ||
children.translated_text: One should cultivate the prior meditations, and then [proceed] to the time of eating. (10)
With this essenceless body, seeking the supreme essence,

children.text: kāyaṃ naukādhiyā rakṣed na bhuṅktāṃ sthūlatākṛte || 11 ||
children.translated_text: one should protect the body with the thought of it as a boat — one should not eat for the sake of corpulence. (11)

children.text: rasāsaktyā na bhuñjīta caturdhānnaṃ vibhajya ca /
children.translated_text: One should not eat out of attachment to taste. Dividing food into four portions,
the first should be offered to the deities, the next to the <s>Dharmapāla</s> (Dharma protector). (12)
A very generous offering should be given; the remainder, after one has eaten and drunk,
should be given to all beings. In the intervals, [one should engage in] discourse and study. (13)
One should relate wondrous accounts. Rising up a little, one should walk about.
One should circumambulate a sacred site, or do recitation or reading of texts. (14)

children.text: sugatapratimāṃ kuryād yāvat svedo na jāyate /
children.translated_text: One should make images of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha). Until perspiration arises,

children.text: kuryāt, pradakṣiṇāṃ tāvad akṣubdhaḥ praṇidhiṃ bahum || 15 ||
children.translated_text: one should perform circumambulations. Unagitated, one should make many aspiration prayers. (15)
Ten dharma-practices have been taught by <s>Maitreya</s>. In brief,
one should practice with an undistracted mind, also recollecting the illusion-like [nature of things]. (16)

children.text: yadi syāt pūjayet saṅghaṃ kuryād vā bālakotsavam /
children.translated_text: If possible, one should worship the <s>Saṃgha</s>, or hold a festival for children.
Generous giving to the destitute is a merit-accumulation for the <s>yogin</s>. (17)

children.text: pūrṇeṣu dinakṛtyeṣu bhāge ca prathame niśaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the daily duties are completed, in the first watch of the night,

children.text: dharmatā niṣprapañcāpi tathā cittaṃ ca yojayet || 18 ||
children.translated_text: one should yoke the mind to the true nature of <s>dharmas</s>, which is beyond conceptual elaboration. (18)
When midnight has arrived, with the perception of luminosity upon awakening,
one should resort to virtuous sleep, like the lion's sleep. (19)
Mainly, when the mind is firm in meditation, physical and verbal merit is secondary.
When in an untouched <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), [one may engage] for the sake of worldly activity. (20)
Physical merit should be [practiced] according to one's capacity. When worldly thought is uneven,
thinking 'this <s>Dharma</s> is not for me alone,' with a thoroughly good intention — (21)
one should inquire into worldly <s>dharmas</s> too, inspired by one's close friends.
[This was] composed in the land of <s>Nepal</s>. If there is no delight in the <s>mantra</s> path — (22)

body.translated_text: thus, O Elder, should one act! (23a)
The <s>Caryāsaṅgrahapradīpa</s> (Lamp of the Summary of Conduct), composed by the great <s>Paṇḍita</s> master <s>Dīpaṅkara Śrījñāna</s>, is complete.
